quick-start.title: Quick start
quick-start.summary: Get an account, see how CoGA is organised, review a first case, and keep the five rules for safe use in mind.
paragraphs: Choose Sign in with Microsoft and use the Microsoft account of your hospital or university. Your first sign-in creates your CoGA account, with the role viewer: you read and change nothing. You see a project's data once an administrator gives you access to it, and you analyse once they give you a higher role.

Where CoGA runs without Microsoft sign-in, choose Sign up on the sign-in page and fill in Create account. You can sign in once an administrator has activated the account and given you access to your projects.

Logout signs you out of CoGA, on every computer and in every browser where you are signed in: each of them asks you to sign in again. On a shared computer, then also choose Sign out of Microsoft on the sign-in page.

The arrow at the right of the top bar opens a menu of the main sections: the projects, the explorers, the gene panels, this guide and, for superusers and administrators, Admin. Settings in the same bar holds your display preferences.
CoGA keeps the pedigree, the assay data and your interpretation together, so you review a case as a whole:
To set up a new case, see Case setup and data import.
blocks: Your role decides what you may do, lowest first: a viewer reads; an analyst also analyses (reviews, tags, classifications, HPO terms, the case's workflow); a supervisor also signs an analysis out; a superuser also has every project and the configuration the analyses read (gene panels, tags, preset filters, QC thresholds) and package import; an admin has the whole administration.

A project decides who sees the data and which reference assembly applies. You see only the projects you belong to; superusers and administrators see everything, and administrators create the projects. In each of your projects you are an analyst, who reads and changes its records as far as your role allows, or a reader, who only reads them. A family page says Read-only access where you only read: your role is viewer, or you are a reader there.
A family is the case: related samples with their pedigree, roles and affected status.
A sample carries the assay data: variants, coverage, segments, repeats and more.
Reference data (genes, cytobands, ClinVar, gnomAD, clinical CNVs and more) belongs to an assembly and is shared by all projects on it.
Review state — classifications, tags and notes — is your interpretation, kept per family.

Use CoGA safely. Decision support only. Review every suggestion, ranking and call; CoGA makes no diagnosis. Screening needs confirmation. Confirm an at-risk NIPT or carrier-screening finding with a diagnostic test. Validated scope only. A family marked Not validated for clinical use is outside the validated assembly (GRCh38) and cannot be signed out. Check Sample QC before sign-out: it confirms that the samples are who the pedigree says. Sign-out closes the analysis. It is the analytical sign-off, not the medical one: the clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the EPD and refers to the signed version. Only a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator signs out; the laboratory decides who gets the supervisor role.

Only a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator signs out; the laboratory decides who gets the supervisor role.
On the dashboard, search for a project, family or sample, and open the family.
On the family page, pick the analysis that fits the question. A button appears only when the family has that kind of data.
Check Sample QC before you interpret.
Build a shortlist in the variant list before you open the viewers.
Record your interpretation as you go: classification, tags and notes.
Tag the variants to report with Report, check the drafted report, and have a supervisor sign out the analysis. The clinical report follows in the EPD.

Not finding a variant you expect? The Small variants page opens with a default filter: the Phenotype priority preset on the Mendeliome panel (rare, HIGH or MODERATE impact, carried by the affected members). Press Clear all filters before you conclude that a variant is missing. The Variant explorer leaves out imputed calls unless you tick Include imputed variants.

case-setup.title: Case setup and data import
case-setup.summary: Create a family, import a data package, and know what each kind of data unlocks.
paragraphs: Choose the way in that matches how your data arrives.
blocks: Build a new family by hand: add samples, set sex and roles, link parents and couples, and set affected and carrier status. Open to the analysts of a project whose role is analyst or higher, who add families to it, and to superusers and administrators; uploading a PED file here is for administrators.
A superuser or an administrator checks, corrects and approves the family folder a pipeline delivers to the CoGA server, or adds a folder by hand, and imports the family with all its data in one job.

Package import is for superusers and administrators. The rest of loading data is for administrators: single uploads on the Upload family and sample data page, and replacing an existing family, by a package import with Overwrite too. So is editing an existing family's members or structure. HPO terms are added, changed and removed by the analysts of the family's project (role analyst or higher), by superusers and by administrators.
For a monogenic NIPT case, tick Monogenic NIPT (cfDNA from maternal plasma) in the family builder: see Monogenic NIPT.

Each kind of data switches on part of CoGA: small variants: the small-variant page and Sample QC; structural variants: the SV page; TRGT calls: the repeat page; Paraphase: the paralogue page; mitochondrial calls: the mtDNA analysis; coverage, segments, APCAD and haplotypes: the viewer tracks. Any variant data also switches on the variant summary.
small variants: the small-variant page and Sample QC;
coverage, segments, APCAD and haplotypes: the viewer tracks.
Any variant data also switches on the variant summary.

Reference data first. Genes, cytobands, ClinVar and the other annotation layers are loaded per assembly. If a viewer cannot place coordinates or a gene search is empty, check that the reference data for the family's assembly is loaded.

phenotype-matching.title: Phenotypes, panels and phenotype matching
phenotype-matching.summary: Record HPO terms, focus a search with a gene panel, and match the phenotype to genes and diseases with Monarch.
paragraphs: The patient's phenotype drives the ranking. Record it as HPO terms, and use gene panels to focus a search.
HPO terms are kept per person. An analyst of the family's project (role analyst or higher), a superuser or an administrator adds them:

Only present terms are used for matching. Each term added, changed or removed is an entry on the family's Clinical audit trail. A package import can bring terms in too: what it adds or changes is one entry per person, naming who ran the import and the package. A viewer or a reader sees the terms but cannot change them.

The Panel catalog holds reusable gene lists. Superusers and administrators create them or import them from PanelApp. To limit a search to a panel's genes, choose the panel in the Locations filter of the small-variant or structural-variant page.

The Mendeliome is the default scope of both pages: every gene that Monarch says causes a disease or is associated with one. A gene that Monarch links to a disease only as contributing to it or raising its likelihood is not in it.
On the small-variant and structural-variant pages and in the variant explorer, a panel of any size keeps:
So the Mendeliome, too, keeps a variant inside one of its genes whose annotation names another gene.
A gene name that no loaded assembly knows, such as a typo or an old symbol, gets no position. The panel's page lists it as not imported: a filter on the panel finds no variant in it.

Superusers and administrators change a local panel's genes on its page, in three ways that can be combined: the bin on a gene's row, Add to changes for new names, and Edit the whole list. Each change is listed under Changes for version N, where a name no assembly knows is flagged. Nothing is saved until you press Confirm and save version N; the earlier version stays in the version history. If someone saved another version in the meantime, CoGA refuses the save, reloads the panel and keeps your changes listed, to confirm again.
CoGA uses the Monarch Initiative knowledge graph, which links genes, diseases and HPO phenotypes.
An administrator loads the Monarch data about monthly (Admin → Monarch data). Until it is loaded, the gene profile shows no associations and the ranking has no phenotype signal.
blocks: Click the person's sample name on the family page.
Under HPO Phenotypes, search a term and choose present, absent or unknown.
Press Add phenotype. Edit changes a term's status or note: choose the new ones and press Save change. Remove takes a term off; to use another term, remove it and add that one.
the variants annotated with one of its genes;
the variants inside one of its regions: PanelApp's regions for the assembly, and each gene's position in the gene reference. A structural variant counts when it overlaps one.

On the gene profile (gene explorer), Monarch gene–disease associations lists each linked disease with its relationship, source and number of expected phenotypes. Opened from a family, it also says how many the family shows ("3 observed in family").

On the family page, the Phenotype match (Monarch) panel ranks candidate genes when you press Find candidate genes. It sends the HPO terms of every family member, not only the affected ones. Re-run match runs it again on the phenotypes recorded now, for example after you add one.
In the variant list, the Phenotype priority preset ranks variants partly by how well their gene matches the affected members' phenotypes (see Small-variant prioritisation).

Record specific phenotypes. A broad term such as Intellectual disability is linked to over a thousand genes and gives a weak ranking by design. Add the patient's distinctive features — a particular seizure type, a dysmorphic feature, a metabolic finding — and the ranking sharpens.

family-workspace.title: The family page
family-workspace.summary: The case hub: status and assignment, one button per analysis and viewer, the region of interest, and the family members.
paragraphs: Every case starts on its family page.

The family page, every analysis page (small and structural variants, repeat expansions, Paraphase, mtDNA, monogenic NIPT, the variant summary), the Sample QC and the report share one header. From any of them you can work on the case and move between analyses.

A row of links at the foot of the header leads to the family's analyses: Small variants, Structural variants, Repeat expansions, Paraphase, mtDNA analysis, Monogenic NIPT and, last, Variant summary (of all the family's variant data). At the far right of the same row, under the pedigree, are the family-level functions: Sample QC (when the family has small variants) and Report (when it has any variant data: small or structural variants, repeat expansions, Paraphase results or mtDNA data). A link appears only when the family has that kind of data. The page you are on is marked.

The ROI is the gene or locus the case is about; PGT uses it for the embryo calls. An administrator sets it (Save, Clear). Anyone can click it to open the chromosome view with 1 Mb on each side. In a PGT family, Review ROI markers → opens the marker review.
One row per person: role, parents, partner, Related to, status, HPO terms and a Seq. QC chip. The chip shows the sequencing QC verdict and mean depth; hover or focus it for the metrics.
In a PGT family each embryo also shows its derived call (see Haplotype segregation).

Related to names the member through whom a person is related by an unknown degree: for example a PGT index known to be on the mother's side, or both parents. The pedigree draws the link as a dotted arc with a ?. The haplotype track colours such a person:
Only an administrator edits a member:

In the same dialog, an analyst of the family's project (role analyst or higher), a superuser or an administrator adds and removes HPO terms. Affected status and carrier status are separate: an unaffected person can be a carrier. Remove member in the dialog takes the person out of the family at once, after you confirm. Members are added in Admin → Family & sample data.
Further down are the Phenotype match (Monarch) panel and, closed by default, the Analysis pipeline settings recorded at import.
blocks: One line gives the members, the assembly and the projects, then the page's own figures.

Status, Assigned to and Reviewed by track the case's workflow. An analyst of the family's project (role analyst or higher), a superuser or an administrator can change them; a viewer and a reader only see them.

Assigned to and Reviewed by offer the active analysts of the family's projects whose role is not viewer, the superusers and the administrators; never a reader or a viewer. Someone chosen before they became a reader or a viewer (or left the family's projects) stays shown, marked (not eligible), until you change it.
The one you choose under Assigned to gets an e-mail naming the family, with a link to it, when a mail server is set; not when you assign the family to yourself.
Read-only access in the header means you only read this family: your role is viewer, or you are a reader in its project.
A Not validated for clinical use banner shows when the family is outside the validated scope.

Curation gives one line each for the small variants, the structural variants, the repeat loci and the Paraphase regions: how many are reviewed, how many carry notes, and the count per review tag. For the repeat loci and the Paraphase regions it also counts how many carry your classification.
Visualization — Genome view, Chromosome view, Circos plot and IGV viewer.
A passing chip shows the number alone. Any other state is a word on the chip.
Warning or Fail: a metric crossed its limit, which the tooltip names.
Not run: the sample's QC was not assessed (no limit set for any of its metrics, or no verdict returned). This is never a pass.
An embryo whose QC holds only the PGT pipeline's embryo metrics has no depth to show. Its chip gives the value of the metric that decided the verdict (Fail ADO 14.2%), or Not run alone.
along the genome, when they turn out to be that member's own parent or child (they share one of the member's haplotypes along nearly every chromosome);
around the ROI only, when they are a more distant relative: there the markers on both sides show the haplotype they share. Elsewhere such a relative stays grey.
Click the sample name to open Family member details.
Change the fields and press Apply to pending.
Press Save pending updates on the family page.

sample-qc.title: Sample-integrity QC
sample-qc.summary: Check, before you interpret, that the samples are who the pedigree says: swaps, wrong relationships, wrong sex and consanguinity.
paragraphs: Open a family and press Sample QC to check that the samples are who the pedigree says. A swapped tube, a wrong parent, a mislabelled sex or unexpected relatedness quietly invalidates everything downstream, so run it before you interpret.

It does not measure contamination. Some results can be a sign of it, among other causes: a high Mendelian-error rate, or heterozygous calls on a man's X that leave his genetic sex indeterminate or female. A pass does not rule contamination out.
The page first works out what kind of case it is and runs only the checks that fit:
blocks: Long-read WGS family — sex, relatedness against the pedigree, Mendelian errors.
Shallow-WGS PGT — embryo sex and parentage (each embryo a child of both parents), Mendelian errors.
Monogenic NIPT — paternity, fetal sex, parent sex and a check of the cfDNA categories.
Carrier couple — sex per partner, and that the two are unrelated.
Overall verdict — the worst of the checks. A check that could not run counts as a warning, never as a pass. A note names each sample whose sex could not be checked.
Pedigree — each person's symbol carries a ring and a badge: green ✓ pass, amber ! warning, red ✕ fail. A check that could not run counts as a warning here too. Hover a symbol for the reason.

Per-sample table — recorded sex against genetic sex, and the Mendelian-error rate. The genetic sex carries green ✓ when it matches the record, red ✗ when it does not, amber ! when it could not be confirmed and grey ? when it was not checked. Hover a cell for the reason. A sample without X genotypes (for example in a PGT family) is sexed from its reads by the pipeline's ngs-bits; the reason says so. An embryo's recorded sex comes from that same call, so its ✓ confirms nothing independent. Nor does the ✓ of an index added with the sex ngs-bits read.
Relatedness matrix — each pair's inferred relationship, kinship and IBS0. A pair that contradicts the pedigree, including parents who look related, is outlined: red for a fail, amber for a warning.
NIPT cards — paternity, fetal sex and the category check, for a cfDNA family.

Sequencing & embryo QC — under its own heading in the per-sample table: each sample's sequencing QC as its pipeline reported it, one column per measure. These are mean depth and alignment and, for a PGT embryo, its allele drop-out (ADO) and drop-in (ADI) and its Mendelian concordance with its parents before and after imputation: the numbers of the pipeline's dashboard. A value outside the lab's cut-off shows its verdict; a value without a cut-off is shown, not judged. Seq. QC is the sample's worst. These values do not change the sample's status or the overall verdict, and do not stop sign-out. The signed report records every value.

What to do with a warning or a fail. A fail points to a real problem: re-check the sample sheet, the pedigree and the genotypes before you interpret. A warning usually means too little data to decide (few informative sites, a low fetal fraction, a check that could not run); it weakens the analysis but does not invalidate it. A fail, or a check of the pedigree or of a sample's identity that could not run (a NIPT parent's sex, for example), also stops sign-out until someone records a reason.
inline: What to do with a warning or a fail.

small-variant-filtering.title: Small-variant prioritisation
small-variant-filtering.summary: The small-variant page: the default view, the filters and presets, the phenotype-driven ranking, and genes also hit by a structural variant.
paragraphs: Most candidates are found on the Small variants page. The filters take a genome down to a short list; the Phenotype priority preset puts it in order.
The page opens with the Phenotype priority (Exomiser-style) preset on the Mendeliome panel:

The filters sit under Advanced filters, grouped as on the screen: Phenotype, Structural second hit, Inheritance, Pathogenicity, Annotations, In silico, Frequency, Call quality, Locations, Exclude and Review and curation.

For de novo and dominant, a male's call on chrX or chrY outside the pseudo-autosomal regions (1 or 1/1) counts as one copy. A location entry that cannot be read (for example an end before its start) is named under its field, and nothing is searched until you fix it. A per-sample minimum (GQ, DP, AF or AD alt) that is not a number fails the search, and the message names it.

The annotation filters must all hold on one transcript of the variant: impact and consequence, the transcript, HGVS, Canonical only, MANE only and LoF only, the ClinVar status, the in-silico scores and the frequencies. So with MANE only and HIGH impact, a variant whose HIGH-impact transcript is not its MANE transcript is left out.

A card, a table row and a CSV row describe one transcript of the variant: MANE Select, else the canonical one, else the most severe. The filters may have held on another. For example, deleterious keeps a variant whose MANE transcript SIFT calls tolerated when a second transcript is deleterious; HIGH or MODERATE impact keeps one that is synonymous on its MANE transcript and missense on another. In that case:
The ranking and ACMG classify read the transcript the row describes.

The built-in presets are Phenotype priority, Dominant strict, Dominant relaxed, Expanded carrier screening, Compound het, Recessive hom, Recessive broad, Any affected and ClinVar review. A preset saves the recipe, not the result; save your own to standardise a search. Compound-heterozygous candidates are shown as pairs. Up to 100 matches show as cards, more as a table.

Under its heading, a card names up to three diseases its gene is linked to: Monarch's causal links, those more sources back first; else the gene's OMIM diseases; else Monarch's associations, marked not causal. +N more opens More annotations & detail, which lists every Monarch and OMIM link. No gene–disease link cached means CoGA's copy of Monarch and OMIM holds none for the gene.
Expanded carrier screening is for couples only. It keeps:

A ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic call overrides the frequency cut-off, so a common founder variant stays in. A partner whose sex is not recorded counts as female. Mitochondrial variants are not part of it, as mtDNA passes from the mother alone.

Your saved searches are shared with the monogenic NIPT page. A search saved there can carry filters that only the NIPT list applies: an inheritance view such as De novo in the fetus, the maternal/fetal categories, the minimum confidence. This page does not send them and shows no chip for them; it names them once under the active filters. De novo in the fetus is not De novo / dominant, which reads the family members' own genotypes.

With Phenotype priority on, a Score column appears and the rows are ranked, best first. The score combines the variant's own evidence (impact and predictors, ClinVar, rarity, fit with the pedigree) with how well its gene matches the affected members' HPO terms. A ✦ marks a gene that matches. Hover the score, or read the card, for the breakdown: Variant, Pathogenicity, Rarity and Phenotype, the compatible inheritance modes and the matched phenotypes.

Why the ranking can be instant. CoGA stores a ranking once computed; a later open shows ⚡ Prioritised ranking served from cache and when it was computed. It is recomputed automatically when anything it depends on changes: the phenotypes, the pedigree, the panel's genes and regions, the filters (including review-tag filters), the family's variant data, or the reference data (the Monarch release, each import of the HPO ontology, gene constraint, and the gene positions a panel or an excluded gene uses).

Narrowing from the Mendeliome to a smaller panel reuses the broader ranking, ranked from 1 within the smaller panel, as long as the Mendeliome's genes and regions have not changed since that ranking was computed. The smaller panel gets its own ranking instead when it reaches a variant the broader ranking lacks (through a region of its own, such as the position PanelApp gives for a gene), or keeps one variant of a compound-het pair without the other.
Download CSV exports the list, with Priority and Rank columns when the ranking is on. Its Classification column holds the class each review shows on the page; Tags holds the review's tags.

A small variant whose gene is also hit by an SV carries an SV badge (for example SV: DEL), with a trans or cis chip when a phase was decided. Also hit by an SV, under Structural second hit, keeps only these genes. The phase comes from read phasing or from the parents' genotypes, by the same rule as for compound-het pairs; the reference gives the rule. Each SV of the gene gets its own phase, listed in the badge's explanation. A deletion in trans with the SNV marks the gene effectively biallelic, whatever the other SVs are.
blocks: gnomAD exome, genome and popmax frequency 1% or below, and at most 10 homozygotes and 10 hemizygotes — a ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic record overrides these cut-offs;
ClinVar benign and likely benign left out;
carried (het or hom) by each affected member, with genotype quality (GQ) 20, depth 10, allele balance 0.2 and 4 alt reads or more.

The default view hides variants. A variant outside the Mendeliome, a common variant, a low-quality call, or a variant an affected member does not carry is not shown. Press Clear all filters before you conclude that a variant is not in the data.

Annotations groups the VEP consequences as seqr does: nonsense, essential splice site, frameshift, missense, in frame, synonymous, extended splice site, other, motif feature and regulatory feature. A group's own box ticks or clears all its terms. Beside them are the VEP impacts (HIGH, MODERATE, LOW, MODIFIER), the SpliceAI minimum, and Canonical only, MANE only and LoF only. A saved search's term that no box offers is listed under Other selected terms, ticked. Its Quick choice sets the consequences and the impacts together, and leaves the SpliceAI minimum and the three switches as they are. All clears both. High impact ticks HIGH, and Moderate to high impact HIGH and MODERATE, with no consequence. All coding ticks the coding consequences (missense, frameshift, stop gained, stop lost, start lost, splice acceptor, donor and region, in-frame insertion and deletion, protein altering, synonymous and coding sequence variant), with no impact. Any other selection shows as Custom.

Its Quick choice sets the consequences and the impacts together, and leaves the SpliceAI minimum and the three switches as they are. All clears both. High impact ticks HIGH, and Moderate to high impact HIGH and MODERATE, with no consequence. All coding ticks the coding consequences (missense, frameshift, stop gained, stop lost, start lost, splice acceptor, donor and region, in-frame insertion and deletion, protein altering, synonymous and coding sequence variant), with no impact. Any other selection shows as Custom.

Frequency has a slider per population. In its header, AF sets every population at once; AC and H/H set gnomAD's allele count and its homozygote and hemizygote counts. AF shows the maximum shared by the populations that have one, or mixed when they differ.

Call quality sets the minimum genotype quality, allele balance, depth and alt reads of the members' calls, for all members at once or per member. With Affected only on, only the affected members' calls are held to them, so a parent's reference call is not held to an allele balance it cannot have. Switched off, every member gets the minimums the affected members share. Pass variants only, under Filter value, keeps a variant when every member's call that carries it passed its caller's FILTER (PASS, or no filter set), whatever Affected only says. Only the family's members count: a sample taken out of the family, or not yet added, holds nothing back. A callset of one file per sample gives each call its own FILTER, so a parent's reference call (DeepVariant's RefCall) holds nothing back. A multi-sample VCF gives the FILTER of the site. The quick choices High quality and Passing turn it on, as in seqr; All variants turns it off.

With Affected only on, only the affected members' calls are held to them, so a parent's reference call is not held to an allele balance it cannot have. Switched off, every member gets the minimums the affected members share.

Pass variants only, under Filter value, keeps a variant when every member's call that carries it passed its caller's FILTER (PASS, or no filter set), whatever Affected only says. Only the family's members count: a sample taken out of the family, or not yet added, holds nothing back. A callset of one file per sample gives each call its own FILTER, so a parent's reference call (DeepVariant's RefCall) holds nothing back. A multi-sample VCF gives the FILTER of the site.
The quick choices High quality and Passing turn it on, as in seqr; All variants turns it off.

Review and curation keeps a variant by the class its review, or its compound-het pair's review, shows. A class word typed as the classification (VUS) gives its class; otherwise the review's class tag gives it, the most severe of two; otherwise the classification as typed. So Likely pathogenic - class 4 also finds a variant classified by its class tag alone, and not one classified as VUS - class 3 beside the Pathogenic - class 5 tag: that variant shows class 5. Capitals do not matter.

Under In silico, one of the predictors you set is enough. The SpliceAI minimum, set under Annotations, counts as one of them. A SpliceAI score at that minimum also passes the impact and consequence filter.

A SIFT or PolyPhen choice keeps a transcript whose prediction is exactly that one, whatever score VEP wrote after it. deleterious keeps deleterious(0.01) but not deleterious_low_confidence(0.03), which is a choice of its own; tolerated leaves out tolerated_low_confidence.

The gene, the rsID and the excluded ClinVar statuses apply to the variant as a whole. A gene keeps every variant annotated with it, including one VEP places just outside the gene (upstream or downstream), ranked or not.

the card (under its transcript) and the table row (under its effect) say Filters met on, with the transcript the filters held on and its consequence, LoF and in-silico predictions that differ from the row's. The row's own values stay as they are;
the card's transcript list marks that transcript Filters met;
the CSV gives it in its last columns, Filter-matched transcript to Filter-matched PolyPhen.
MANE only needs GRCh38. MANE only keeps a variant with a MANE Select or MANE Plus Clinical transcript. VEP sets these flags on GRCh38 only, so on a GRCh37 or T2T family MANE only keeps nothing.
the genes where both partners carry a rare (below 1%) high- or moderate-impact variant;
the variants a female partner carries on chrX outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, which put a son at risk on their own.

A search can stop part-way. Compound-het and recessive pairing and Expanded carrier screening read at most 5,000 candidates before they filter, ranked or not. When a search reaches that limit, a warning above the results says "Results may be incomplete" and after how many candidates the search stopped. The count is then a lower bound (for example 12+), and a match beyond the limit is not shown. Narrow the filters with a region, a gene panel or a gene until the warning is gone.
A gene without Monarch data gets no phenotype credit and ranks lower; its Variant score is not affected. Look further down for strong variants, or untick Phenotype prioritization.
Without HPO terms on the affected members, the ranking uses the variant evidence only.

The ranking changes the order of a search, not what it finds. With an inheritance mode or Expanded carrier screening it ranks the same variants and compound-het pairs the search finds without it. A pair stays a pair, listed where its better-ranked variant ranks; each variant shows its own rank.
The score orders candidates within the family; it is not a probability of pathogenicity.

A warning that "Ranking may be incomplete" means more candidates matched than CoGA ranks at once (it says how many were ranked), so the best one may be missing. Narrow the filters: a region, a panel, a gene, or a tighter frequency or impact.
Also hit by a structural variant

interpretation-and-review.title: Interpretation and review
interpretation-and-review.summary: Tag, annotate and classify variants — with the semi-automatic ACMG classifier — and keep the review state per family.
paragraphs: Record your interpretation as you go. Review state is kept per family: the same variant in two families has two separate records.

Each row or card has Review, Exclude and Report (one-click tags), Tags & notes and ACMG classify. An excluded variant stays in the list. Its card folds to its heading and a bar marked Excluded: Show card unfolds it, and Undo exclude takes the tag off again. In the table view its row is dimmed.
ACMG classify opens a dialog that pre-evaluates the ACMG/AMP criteria from the variant, the gene and the family genotypes, and scores them on the ClinGen points scale.
A variant opened from the mtDNA analysis page gets a mitochondrial rule set.

The structural-variant page works the same way: Review, Exclude, Report, tags and notes, and ACMG (CNV) for the ClinGen copy-number classifier. Saving a CNV classification also freezes its evidence, so the report can tell whether it changed. An event called by more than one caller is listed once per caller, with one shared review; the classification freezes the evidence of the row you opened it from. Small-variant and SV review are counted separately on the family page.
blocks: Tags. The built-in tags are Review, Send for validation, Validated, Validation did not confirm, Confident AR single hit, Excluded and Report, the ACMG class tags, the VUS tiers and Secondary finding. A superuser or an administrator can add custom tags for one project or for everyone. A renamed custom tag stays on every review that holds it. A deleted one stays too, marked (deleted): untick it to remove it from a review. It can no longer be added.

Class. A row or card shows the review's class once. A class word typed as the classification (VUS) gives its class; otherwise the review's class tag gives it, the most severe of two; otherwise the classification as typed. A class tag of another class is not shown beside it. The VUS tiers and Secondary finding are tags, never the class. The filters, the Variant Explorer and Download CSV read the class the same way.

Review, Exclude and Report change the tags only: the classification stays as stored. Tags & notes opens on the class shown. Choosing another class there, or none, replaces the classification and every class tag; left alone, the save keeps both as they are.
Notes keep your reasoning with the variant.
Report puts the variant in the family report.

Each criterion shows as checked (the data supports it), ● (consider), ✕ (the data argues against) or n/a (cannot apply). Hover it for the evidence; click to change it, and pick its strength. Only checked criteria count.
The bar at the top shows the points, the class and, for a VUS, the tier (hot, warm or cold).
The header links to gnomAD, ClinVar, DECIPHER and a PubMed search on the gene and the patient's HPO terms.

Save classification stores the class as the variant's classification and review tag, with every criterion and your note; the server recomputes the class. It also freezes the evidence the dialog read — the ClinVar significance, the consequence and LoF call, the population frequencies, the in-silico scores and, for a missense variant, the gene's missense Z — so the report can later tell whether it changed, and what.
Opening a classified variant again shows the criteria as you saved them.
Decision support, not an autoclassifier. The dialog pre-positions the criteria; you confirm them, adjust the strengths and add a note.

clinical-report.title: Family report and sign-out
clinical-report.summary: Draft the family report from the tagged variants, see what changed, and sign the analysis out into a version that can never change. The clinical report is signed in the EPD.
paragraphs: Tag a variant with Report to add it to the family report (the Report button on the family page). The live report drafts text per reported variant — description, ACMG reasoning, gene context and phenotype overlap — and is where you sign out the analysis. After sign-out, the Report button opens the signed version.

Sign-out closes the analysis; the medical sign-off is in the EPD. Sign out report is the analytical sign-off: it closes the analysis and freezes it into a signed version. The clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the hospital's electronic patient record (EPD), not in CoGA. It refers to exactly one signed version: the one it rests on.
Sign out report freezes the reported result into a numbered version with a unique fingerprint. The version also holds what the analysis looked at:
The EPD refers to the signed version by its report code (for example 7KQM2X-2-4PHT). Sign-out stops for seven things:

Your acknowledgement covers exactly what its dialog lists. If the concerns change before you click Sign out anyway, nothing is signed out: the dialog shows the current concerns, says they changed, and asks for your reason again.

A PGT embryo call whose phasing QC does not meet its thresholds (⚠ phasing QC on the family page) does not stop sign-out: the call stands, you decide on it, and the signed version records the warning.

Every reason you give is frozen into the signed version and written to the audit trail. Signing out again (Amend sign-out) creates a new version; earlier versions are never overwritten. A clinical report that rests on the amended analysis refers to the new version. After sign-out the page shows the signed version and its report code: quote that code in the EPD report. A mistyped code is refused as a typo, never taken for another record's. Report codes in the main menu finds the signed version a code names.

Only the signed version is. A signed case opens on its latest signed version, drawn from the frozen record: Signed version N — signed out by … on …, with its report code and fingerprint. It shows what was signed:

It says what the record does not hold — the population frequencies and predictions, the gene and phenotype context, the audit trail — and never fills that in from current data. Print signed version N prints it; Download signed version N (JSON) returns the record itself. Signed versions lists the earlier ones.

Open the live report shows the current data. It says This is the live report, not signed version N, and whether it still matches: amber when something changed since (it names what), grey when the check could not be made (treat it as unsigned). Its printout starts with Not the signed report.
blocks: Every reported variant, small and structural. If a list cannot hold them all, an Incomplete warning says so, on screen and in print, so a printout cannot pass for the whole list.

Each variant's class as the family page shows it: a class word in the classification (VUS), else its class tag, else the text. When the ACMG classification, or a structural variant's CNV scoring, gives another class, that score stands beside it: VUS - class 3 (ACMG score: Likely pathogenic - class 4 · 8 pts). A structural variant whose review shows no class reads Not classified, even with a CNV score.

The repeat expansions and Paraphase findings marked Report: gene and disease, every member's call with CoGA's status, your classification and note, and the marks differs from CoGA's status and Changed since review where they apply. Without any, the section says so.

A provenance footer, printed with the report: the CoGA version that produced the page, the in-house IVD statement and the manufacturer, and the versions behind the data (the pipeline tools, the assembly, the gene loci, the Monarch release and the HPO release).

An evidence-drift banner when a classification's evidence changed after it was made: for example a new ClinVar significance, REVEL score or gnomAD frequency (REVEL 0.412 → 0.951), consequence or LoF call (LoF LC → HC), missense Z for a missense variant's gene, or a structural variant that now overlaps other genes. Re-review those variants.

The Clinical audit trail: who classified, tagged or annotated what, who reviewed a compound-heterozygous pair, who changed the pedigree or the family's phenotypes, and when. Entries can never be changed or deleted. Only analysts, superusers and administrators see it; a viewer, or a reader of the family's project, sees on screen and in print that it is not shown. It opens on the 200 most recent entries; when there are more, it says how many it shows, and Show older events loads the next 200. A printout of only part of the trail says so.
The Analysis pipeline settings recorded at import.

An Import incomplete warning at the top when a data import left the family partly loaded or has not finished (still running, or stopped part-way, for example by a server restart). It names the import job and the datasets that failed or were not finished. It also names: a single upload that has not finished, or that failed and could not put back what it deleted, as a single-file upload; an unfinished deletion of the family's data, as a deletion of this family's data: an administrator's deletion of a sample or of the family, a PED upload that replaces the family, or a structure change that clears its data. The warning shows on every family page until an import or an upload has brought those datasets again.
a single upload that has not finished, or that failed and could not put back what it deleted, as a single-file upload;

an unfinished deletion of the family's data, as a deletion of this family's data: an administrator's deletion of a sample or of the family, a PED upload that replaces the family, or a structure change that clears its data.

A Package folder changed after import warning at the top when the folder the family was imported from has changed since its import, naming the files added, removed or changed; or Package folder gone when it is gone or cannot be read, so the read files, signal tracks and QC report shown from it are no longer available. It shows until the folder is as it was imported again, or its new delivery is imported or refused with a reason.
each reported variant's description as you reviewed it;
the gene panels the family's searches applied;

the repeat-expansion and Paraphase results, with each repeat count near a boundary marked, TRGT's own count beside a count QA's correction changed, and each locus's correction and whether QA had validated TRGT's counting units there;
what each coverage track held (read depth, a log2 ratio or unknown), and whether an upload or a package loaded it;
in a PGT family, each embryo's call at the region of interest as the family page shows it, with its phasing QC and that QC's verdict against the thresholds;
in a monogenic NIPT family, its NIPT results (the NIPT report uses this same sign-out; see the NIPT chapter).
An assembly outside the validated scope (Not validated for clinical use): the report cannot be signed out.
Data being written: a data import of the family is queued or running, or an upload or a deletion of its variants is changing its data. Sign out once it has finished; there is no override.

Evidence drift of a small variant, a structural variant or a CNV, including a reported variant never saved through ACMG classify or ACMG (CNV) (its evidence cannot be checked), and of a repeat or Paraphase review with a classification or the Report tag whose calls changed since. Re-review, or acknowledge with a reason. The dialog lists each classification and what moved.

Sample QC that failed or could not confirm the pedigree or a sample's identity, and, for a NIPT family, a failed NIPT quality check: acknowledge with a reason. Before you write it, the dialog lists every concern under its own heading: failed checks, checks that could not run, failed NIPT quality checks, and warnings (which do not stop sign-out on their own). Each concern names the sample, pair or child it is about; your reason covers all of them.

An incomplete import (Import incomplete): import what failed again, or acknowledge with a reason. After an import that stopped part-way, re-run it with overwrite: an update skips data that is already there, partly written data too. After a failed overwrite that could not put the family's data back, import the whole family again with overwrite (every dataset the warning names, not only the failed ones), and upload again with overwrite what an upload brought. After an unfinished single upload or deletion, upload or import again with overwrite what the warning names. After an administrator's unfinished deletion of a sample, deleting the sample again also removes what the warning names of it.

After an administrator's unfinished deletion of a sample, deleting the sample again also removes what the warning names of it.

A changed package folder (Package folder changed after import, or gone): import or refuse the folder's new delivery, or acknowledge with a reason. The dialog lists the files that changed; the signed version keeps them with your reason.

Repeat and Paraphase calls without a review (no tag, note or classification at the locus or region): a repeat call reading Pathogenic, Premutation, Review or Not assessed, a count Near a boundary, or a Paraphase call reading pathogenic, carrier or review. Review it, or acknowledge with a reason. A grey-zone call alone does not stop sign-out.

Only a supervisor signs out. Sign out report is for a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator. For an analyst, a viewer or a reader the button is disabled and says why, and CoGA refuses the sign-out. The laboratory decides who gets the supervisor role; CoGA records who signed. The medical sign-off is given in the EPD.
each reported variant's description, classification, criteria, evidence and note. The class is the one its review showed when you signed, with the ACMG or CNV score beside it as on the live report;
in a PGT family, the embryo calls (PGT embryo results, with each call's QC verdict and the thresholds);
in a monogenic NIPT family, its NIPT results (NIPT results);

the repeat expansions (each count near a boundary marked beside its call, ⚠ Near a boundary; a corrected count with TRGT's own in brackets, 18 (TRGT 19); and each locus's counting units and correction as QA had recorded them) and Paraphase results;
the coverage tracks (Coverage tracks: what each held, and from which file);
the reference-data releases and the checks at sign-out.

specialised-analyses.title: Structural variants, repeats, Paraphase and mtDNA
specialised-analyses.summary: The analyses beyond small variants, including the CNV classifier and the variant summary.
paragraphs: The Structural variants page opens on the Mendeliome panel, with a population frequency below 1% and the affected members as carriers. Its filters are Phenotype, Inheritance and Support, Locations, Class and Breakpoints, Needlr Annotations and Review; the presets are Mendeliome, Dominant, Recessive-like and Any affected. Phenotype prioritization ranks SVs by the same phenotype score as small variants. Clear all filters removes the default.

Save current keeps your filters as a saved search: for this family, or, with Every family I open (reusable), for each family you open. Your saved searches are listed under the presets. Choose one and Delete saved search removes it; a reusable one goes from every family.

As on the small-variant page, a gene panel of any size keeps an SV whose annotation names one of its genes or that overlaps one of its regions. So the Mendeliome also keeps an SV in one of its genes whose annotation names that gene otherwise, and a small panel an SV annotated with one of its genes that does not overlap it, such as a gene a few kilobases away. With both a gene panel and a Gene symbol filled in, an SV must meet both.

The classification under Review keeps an SV by the class its review shows, as on the small-variant page. A class word typed as the classification (VUS) gives its class; otherwise the review's class tag gives it, the most severe of two; otherwise the classification as typed. A CNV classification counts with the class it saved as the classification. So Likely pathogenic - class 4 also finds an SV classified by its class tag alone, and not one classified as VUS - class 3 beside the Pathogenic - class 5 tag: that SV shows class 5. Capitals do not matter.
Min length and Exact length, under Class and Breakpoints, measure an SV by the Length the list shows, without a deletion's minus sign. That length is:

An insertion is as long as the sequence it inserts, although most callers write its end at its start. A length typed with a minus sign, as the list writes a deletion's, is read without it. A translocation (BND, TRA) has no length: the list shows none, every minimum keeps it, and no exact length finds it.

A filtered search reads at most 50,000 SVs of the callset before it applies the filters. With Phenotype prioritization on (the default) it ranks at most 5,000 of the SVs that match. When a search reaches either limit, a warning says "Results may be incomplete" ("Ranking may be incomplete" when the list is ranked), the count shows a +, and an SV beyond the limit is not shown. Narrow the search with a region, a gene panel or a gene. A gene panel of any size (the Mendeliome included) and a gene are applied before the 50,000 are read, so the limit counts only the SVs they keep. The family report's list of reported SVs is not cut by this limit: it reads the reported SVs themselves, not the first 50,000.
ACMG (CNV) on a row opens the ClinGen copy-number classifier (Riggs et al. 2020): choose Copy-number loss or Copy-number gain, check the pre-selected criteria and add the rest.
The Repeat expansions page lists each repeat locus with every member's call: the repeat count of each allele, and a status read against the locus's thresholds in the repeat catalogue (STRchive):

Aberrant only, ticked when the page opens, keeps every locus whose status is not Normal or Unknown, Not assessed included. The page header counts the calls not assessed. This page and the genome tracks classify every call again, against the catalogue as it is now, and the tracks colour each call by the status the repeat page gives it.
Near a boundary. TRGT counts the motif across the region its own catalogue gives a locus, which need not be the clinical repeat number the locus's ranges count:

Until QA and the laboratory director have validated a locus's counting units, a count within 3 repeats of a boundary the locus's classification uses is marked Near a boundary beside its call. Hover over or focus the mark for the count, the nearest count on each side that reads another status, and what is known of TRGT's count at the gene. The status itself is not changed: read the call with the mark in mind. Aberrant only keeps such a locus whatever its status, the page header counts the calls near a boundary, and a genome track says it in the locus's tooltip.

Count correction. QA can record a correction for a locus, in repeats, on the admin page Repeat catalogue. CoGA adds it to TRGT's count before the count is classified, whether or not the locus is validated. The call then shows the corrected count with TRGT's own in brackets, 17 / 36 (TRGT 18 / 37), and the card's Count correction line says the correction and its reason. The status, the mark, the genome tracks and the signed record all use the corrected count. No locus has a correction until QA enters one.

An administrator records each locus's validation and correction, with a reason, on the admin page Repeat catalogue; a validated locus is no longer marked. Signing out freezes, beside each call, the corrected count, TRGT's own count and the mark, and for each locus QA's record: the correction, whether QA had validated its counting units, the reason, by whom and when. A locus validated, withdrawn or corrected after sign-out makes the report say the repeat expansions changed since.

Some genes lie in regions with nearly identical copies, such as SMN1/SMN2 or PMS2, where standard variant calling fails. The Paraphase page shows, per locus, what Paraphase found there for each member: the copy number, and a status read from a catalogue of medical regions.

Copy-number changes and abnormal calls only, ticked when the page opens, shows the regions with such a change or with a member's call that reads Pathogenic, Carrier or Review: a fusion is reviewed without any change in copy number. Untick it to see every region.

Each repeat locus and Paraphase region has its own review, kept per family and reference assembly. Its card has the controls of every variant card: Review, Exclude and Report toggle their tag, and Tags & notes opens the review. There you give your classification on the type's own scale, beside CoGA's status, which it never changes:

The ACMG class tags and VUS tiers are for small variants and are not offered here. A review that already holds one lists it, marked, so you can untick it. The card shows your classification as Review: …. It adds Differs from CoGA's status when the classification agrees with none of the members' calls (a Normal where every call reads Pathogenic, say). A review is of the locus or region, so a classification that fits one member's call is not marked. Exclude folds the card to its heading; the card stays in the list, Aberrant only included.

CoGA freezes the calls a classification, or the Report tag, rests on when you save it. When the calls change after that (a new import, a locus whose counting units QA validated), the card says Changed since review, and the tooltip names what changed. It says No call since review when the family holds no call there any more. A save of tags or a note alone keeps the calls your classification rests on. Sign-out checks them again (see Clinical report).

On the mtDNA analysis page, each sample's row in the family summary gives its mean chrM depth, the share of chrM covered, and a QC status judged against the lab's limits (Sequencing QC thresholds). The depth comes from one coverage track that holds read depth: the sample's coverage BED when it was declared as read depth, otherwise HiFiCNV's depth where the import stored it as read. These never count: WisecondorX's and QDNAseq's bins, HiFiCNV's normalised depth and a coverage BED declared as a log2 ratio (they hold log2 ratios, not depths), and a coverage BED that does not say what it holds. A sample without a track of read depth shows the depth of its chrM calls, and the page's QC notes name each track left out and why.

Each mtDNA variant has the same review as a small variant, and its card the same controls: Review, Exclude, Report, Tags & notes and ACMG classify. It is one review: the same variant on the Small variants page shows the same tags and note, and Report puts it on the report with the other reported small variants. ACMG classify on a variant from the mtDNA analysis page uses the mitochondrial rule set.

A card links to IGV, the chromosome view, OMIM (for a variant in a gene), MITOMAP and VarSome. VarSome opens the variant on the revised Cambridge Reference Sequence, whatever the family's assembly. A single-base change that alters the protein of one of the 13 protein-coding genes also links to MitImpact, which holds only such changes.

Variant summary, the last link of the family's analyses, describes all the variant data the family holds. It is shown when the family has any. A row of tabs at the top has one tab per kind of data the family has, and the page shows one kind at a time: the first tab opens, and a click on another shows that kind instead. The figures describe the calls. No filter, classification or sign-out reads them.
A tab loads when you first open it, and keeps its figures when you switch away and back. One that could not be loaded says so and offers Retry; the other tabs still work.

Exploratory — not for clinical use. The Ancestry (exploratory) section, at the end of a family's Sample QC, places its individuals beside public reference populations on four principal components: genetic similarity, not an ancestry percentage or an ethnic identity. It is outside CoGA's intended purpose, has not been validated, and is never part of the sign-out or of the signed record. It reads the family's stored GRCh38 callsets, measures whether each covers a genome, an exome or only part of the markers, and is calculated again automatically when the genotypes change. For one individual you can choose another callset, give the regions of a gene panel or a BED file, include an embryo or leave the individual out.
blocks: Filter and review CNVs and other SVs with their genotypes, rank them by phenotype, classify copy-number changes, and tag them for the report.
Per-sample repeat calls, scored against the STRchive catalogue of disease loci.
Genes in paralogous or duplicated regions, where standard variant calling is unreliable.
mtDNA variants and large chrM deletions and duplications, each with its heteroplasmy per member, and each sample's mtDNA coverage.
for a call written as its sequence without an SVLEN (as VCF 4.4 writes one), the bases it inserts or deletes;
otherwise, the end minus the start.

Normal, Grey zone (the intermediate range), Premutation (an FMR1 allele of 55–200 repeats, which can expand in a child) and Pathogenic. Where the catalogue gives a locus a benign range and a pathogenic threshold but no grey zone, a count between the two reads Grey zone: it is neither benign nor pathogenic.
Review: outside catalogued ranges: a count the catalogue cannot classify at a locus that is pathogenic by contraction.
Review: two chrX alleles in a male: a male's call with two different chrX alleles, where he carries one; a note explains it.

Not assessed: a call at a locus without thresholds. No catalogued locus matches its TRID (a locus the catalogue lacks, or a TRID spelled differently), or the catalogue gives the locus no threshold. CoGA cannot say whether such a count is normal; its cutoff reads No reference cutoff. Where the catalogue gives a locus a benign range but no threshold (STRchive's POLG: 10 repeats), a count inside the range reads Normal and any other count Not assessed; the cutoff reads normal 10 · no threshold. The count is the one TRGT reports for the catalogued motif across the whole locus, flanking copies included, so it can run higher than the count the range describes. In the TRGT catalogue in use (TRID CPEO_POLG), POLG's common allele of 10 repeats counts 14 and stays Not assessed.

A gene with several repeat tracts, each a locus of its own in STRchive (ARX, HOXA13), has thresholds per tract. A call whose TRID is the gene's name is read against the tract its region overlaps. If the region overlaps none of the tracts, or more than one, the call reads Not assessed, and its note names the tracts and says why.
at FMR1 it leaves out the AGG interruptions, so an allele reads 1 to 3 below its clinical number (a premutation of 55 repeats can read 53, in the grey zone);
at HTT it also counts the CAG after the CAA interruption, one above the usual count;
at POLG it counts four flanking GCT copies, so the common 10-repeat allele reads 14.
Where the catalogue has a rule for the locus, the copy number reads as normal, carrier or pathogenic, or as review when it fits none of them.

At a locus without a rule, a copy-number change or a fusion reads as review. A change is a copy number outside the normal range the catalogue records for the locus (6 for NEB, 4 for a gene with its pseudogene).
On chrX a man has one copy and a woman two, by the sex Paraphase infers, else the pedigree's. Without a sex, a chrX value is not called normal.
A field without a fixed normal value (highest_total_cn) and a no-call are no change.
Reviewing a repeat locus or a Paraphase region
a repeat locus: Pathogenic expansion, Reduced penetrance, Premutation, Intermediate (grey zone), Normal or Uncertain significance;
a Paraphase region: Affected, Carrier, Risk allele, Normal or Uncertain significance.

NIPT-M, first, for a monogenic NIPT family: the plasma's sites as the NIPT analysis classes them, with the NIPT page's fetal fraction, filters and categories. The plasma's GT is no genotype (Mutect2 writes 0/1 on every call, and the plasma holds the mother's and the fetus's DNA), so the genotypes come from the allele fractions. The fetal fraction, the sites grouped, the fetal sex, paternity, and what the assay's artefact list did: the alleles removed, how many of the alleles it lists are in this family, and those kept in because ClinVar may call them pathogenic or they are common. An empty list says so. Mother and fetus: the groups one under another, by the mother's genotype and then the fetus's, each with its sites and share, the plasma allele fraction its category predicts beside the median observed, and the share classified with a confidence of 0.99 or more. Each group can be split by the father's genotype or the variant class. Plasma allele fraction, in bins of 0.01. Per group gives each group a row on its own scale, so a small group reads as well as a large one, with a dashed line where its category is expected and a triangle at its observed median. All sites stacks the groups, with numbered lines where the categories are expected; a hom/hom peak far above the rest is cut, its full count beside it, so that the other bins can be read (the log scale shows it whole). Peaks off their lines mean the fetal fraction or the classes do not fit. Hover a bin for its sites. Transmission by chromosome: per autosome, the father's het and hom-alt alleles the fetus inherited, the mother's het alleles, and the fetus's hom-alt sites. An autosome where none of a parent's alleles reached the fetus over at least 20 sites is marked: it can point to uniparental disomy or a deletion. CoGA does not call UPD. Calls and the father's genotypes: the plasma calls through the quality filter and the artefact list, the caller's own FILTER (Mutect2's somatic filters flag many germline calls; the analysis does not use them) and the father's genotype from his allele fraction.

The fetal fraction, the sites grouped, the fetal sex, paternity, and what the assay's artefact list did: the alleles removed, how many of the alleles it lists are in this family, and those kept in because ClinVar may call them pathogenic or they are common. An empty list says so.

Mother and fetus: the groups one under another, by the mother's genotype and then the fetus's, each with its sites and share, the plasma allele fraction its category predicts beside the median observed, and the share classified with a confidence of 0.99 or more. Each group can be split by the father's genotype or the variant class.

Plasma allele fraction, in bins of 0.01. Per group gives each group a row on its own scale, so a small group reads as well as a large one, with a dashed line where its category is expected and a triangle at its observed median. All sites stacks the groups, with numbered lines where the categories are expected; a hom/hom peak far above the rest is cut, its full count beside it, so that the other bins can be read (the log scale shows it whole). Peaks off their lines mean the fetal fraction or the classes do not fit. Hover a bin for its sites.

Transmission by chromosome: per autosome, the father's het and hom-alt alleles the fetus inherited, the mother's het alleles, and the fetus's hom-alt sites. An autosome where none of a parent's alleles reached the fetus over at least 20 sites is marked: it can point to uniparental disomy or a deletion. CoGA does not call UPD.

Calls and the father's genotypes: the plasma calls through the quality filter and the artefact list, the caller's own FILTER (Mutect2's somatic filters flag many germline calls; the analysis does not use them) and the father's genotype from his allele fraction.

Small variants (SNV/indel), counted from the family's own callsets. Imputed genotypes (GLIMPSE2) and chrM are left out; chrM is under mtDNA. Each variant counts once, even when two callsets hold it. In a monogenic NIPT family the plasma's and the father's heterozygous and homozygous counts are left out (their GT is no genotype): the NIPT-M tab classes them. Per sample: variants, heterozygous and homozygous, the het/hom ratio, SNVs, insertions, deletions and other changes, the transition/transversion ratio, and the share that passed the caller's FILTER. Consequences: each variant under its most severe consequence over all its transcripts, in the groups of the small-variant filter, with the total in the coding sequence. The small-variant search may name another transcript of the same variant. Per chromosome: each member's heterozygous and homozygous variants, and the homozygous share. Call quality: histograms of each member's genotype quality, depth and, for heterozygous calls, allele balance. These count calls, so a variant two callsets hold counts twice. Mendelian inconsistencies: for each child with both parents in the family, per callset and autosome. It counts the sites where all three have a biallelic diploid call, and those no transmission explains: the father's allele missing, the mother's, or from neither parent. Many inconsistencies on one chromosome that all miss one parent's allele can point to uniparental disomy or a deletion. CoGA does not call UPD: confirm it by another method.
Per sample: variants, heterozygous and homozygous, the het/hom ratio, SNVs, insertions, deletions and other changes, the transition/transversion ratio, and the share that passed the caller's FILTER.

Consequences: each variant under its most severe consequence over all its transcripts, in the groups of the small-variant filter, with the total in the coding sequence. The small-variant search may name another transcript of the same variant.
Per chromosome: each member's heterozygous and homozygous variants, and the homozygous share.
Call quality: histograms of each member's genotype quality, depth and, for heterozygous calls, allele balance. These count calls, so a variant two callsets hold counts twice.

Mendelian inconsistencies: for each child with both parents in the family, per callset and autosome. It counts the sites where all three have a biallelic diploid call, and those no transmission explains: the father's allele missing, the mother's, or from neither parent. Many inconsistencies on one chromosome that all miss one parent's allele can point to uniparental disomy or a deletion. CoGA does not call UPD: confirm it by another method.

Structural variants, from every caller, HiFiCNV's copy-number calls included: per member and type, per chromosome and type, sharing between members, and length histograms. The WisecondorX and QDNAseq segments are coverage tracks, not variants, and are not counted.
Repeat expansions, Paraphase and Mitochondrial DNA: each member's calls by the status its analysis page gives them, and for mtDNA the haplogroup, the mean depth and the heteroplasmy classes.

visualization.title: Genome visualisation
visualization.summary: From a candidate to its context: the genome and chromosome views, Circos and IGV, and how the small-variant and structural-variant tracks are drawn.
paragraphs: Tables are for finding candidates; viewers are for checking them in their genomic context. From the family page:
The IGV and View links on a variant row or card, and the Genome and Circos buttons above the structural-variant table, open in a new browser tab, so your filtered list stays as it was.
In the chromosome view each small variant is drawn by its class, with a legend on the track:

A variant with a conflicting or uncertain ClinVar record is drawn by its impact. A review tag draws a ring in the tag's colour around the mark; the mark itself does not change. Hover a mark for its impact, ClinVar status and parental origin.

When the sample shown has a parent in the family, the track has three rows: variants inherited from the father (top), from the mother (bottom), and of unknown origin (middle: homozygous, de novo or ambiguous). The origin comes from the parents' genotypes when both are there, otherwise from the phased genotype. Without a parent in the family there is one row.
Coverage is drawn as one track per CNV caller, on the axis of what the track holds:

In a PGT family, judge each embryo's aneuploidy and large (>10 Mb) structural variants yourself, on its segment, copy-number (coverage) and APCAD tracks. CoGA shows the tracks but makes no aneuploidy call.

For an aneuploidy, tick Parental origin (aneuploidy) under Tracks in the genome and chromosome views. It is offered for an embryo whose PGT pipeline run wrote its segregation table, and is off until you tick it. It draws the embryo's sites as the pipeline's own plots do, in two panels: Mother heterozygous (the pipeline's group 2: the mother heterozygous, the father homozygous) and Father heterozygous (group 3). Each site is at the embryo's allele fraction, from 0 to 1, coloured by the other parent's homozygous allele: amber for the reference (2B, 3B), the heterozygous parent's colour for the alternate (2A, 3A). The genome view draws every chromosome side by side, so an aneuploid one stands out against the others; the chromosome view draws the region in view. Read each panel against its guide lines:
Read the result against the centromere on the chromosome view's ideogram:

The APCAD track shows which parent gave the extra copy of an isodisomic trisomy. The pipeline keeps only sites the embryo was read deeply at, so a trisomic chromosome has many more sites than the others, and a monosomy almost none. CoGA draws the sites and makes no call from them.
The PGT haplotype track is explained under Haplotype segregation.
The genome and chromosome views draw every SV that the structural-variant list shows, in one of six rows:

A CNV is placed by the copy number stored for the sample's call, as the SV ranking scores it: a male has one copy of chrX and chrY outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, and a CNV without a stored copy number counts as a loss. Hover an SV for its type as the caller wrote it, a CNV's copy-number change, and the call's copy number (CN). The Circos plot draws each SV the same way, from the calls of the whole family.
blocks: Genome view — chromosomes 1–22, X and Y with their variants and tracks. The mitochondrion, too small to see there, is in the chromosome view (chrM) and on the mtDNA analysis page.
Chromosome view — one chromosome with coverage, segments, APCAD, haplotypes and variant tracks. Clicking the ROI on the family page opens it here with 1 Mb on each side.
Circos plot — genome-wide structural relationships at a glance, drawn on chromosomes 1–22, X and Y of the family's assembly. For an assembly it cannot draw, the page says why and draws nothing.
IGV viewer — the reads at a locus, on the genome of the family's assembly. For an assembly it has no genome for, the page says so and opens none, rather than another assembly's genome.

Viewers show only what was imported. A coverage, segment, APCAD or haplotype track appears when that data was loaded for the sample, so an empty track usually means the layer is missing, not that the viewer failed. When a view holds too many variants to draw, the track says so: zoom in or filter.
The callers' log2 ratios share the log2-ratio axis, with the gain and loss colours and the caller's segments.

Read depth is drawn on a depth axis from 0, without those colours or segments. This covers a coverage BED declared as read depth, and a HiFiCNV depth file without autosomal depth: that file gives no baseline to take a ratio against, so its depths are kept as read (the track's header says so).
A coverage BED says what it holds when it is loaded. One that does not is drawn on its own range without an axis, and its header warns that it is read as neither depth nor a log2 ratio.
only ⅓ and ⅔, nothing at 0 or 1
two copies of one of its homologs (isodisomy), or, in a trisomy, the panel of the parent who gave one copy of three
heterodisomy at the centromere points to an error in meiosis I;
isodisomy at the centromere, turning to heterodisomy past a crossover, points to meiosis II;
isodisomy along the whole chromosome points to a mitotic error, usually as a mosaic, where the bands sit between those of a disomy and a trisomy.
Deletions of any subtype (DEL:ME), and CNVs that remove a copy
Duplications of any subtype (DUP:TANDEM), and CNVs that add a copy
Any other type, and CNVs that change no copy number, in grey

haplotype-segregation.title: Haplotype segregation (PGT)
haplotype-segregation.summary: Follow the parental haplotypes through the family to see which embryos inherited the disease haplotype — and when not to trust the call.
paragraphs: The Haplotypes track (chromosome view and genome overview) is CoGA's PGT tool. It colours each person's two haplotypes by the parental homolog they descend from, finds the haplotype that carries the disease allele, and calls each embryo from it.

Each embryo's call is a badge in the Family members table on the family page: Affected / at risk, Carrier, Unaffected or Uninformative. To call an embryo free of a disease haplotype, CoGA needs the embryo's own haplotype across the ROI; without it the embryo reads Uninformative. The server works the calls out from the stored haplotypes. Sign out report freezes the same calls into the signed version (PGT embryo results), each with the haplotypes it rests on, its warnings, its QC at the ROI and that QC's verdict against the thresholds. Next to the badge may be:

Review ROI markers → shows the phased genotypes of every member across the ROI, with each child's Mendelian-error rate. Use it to re-check a surprising call. A single marker that disagrees with its neighbours is noise, not a crossover. A clearly raised Mendelian-error rate points to a swap or a wrong pedigree.
In a single-parent (donor) family the donor lane stays grey, and a recessive call is uninformative because the donor side is unknown.
blocks: Phased imputed genotypes (GLIMPSE2) for the couple, the embryos and the relatives you want coloured.
A correct pedigree, including the grandparents, who anchor the disease haplotype.

Every member's sex, recorded before the phased genotypes are imported. On chrX a man has one X outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, and the haplotypes there are built with the sexes recorded at the import. After recording or correcting a sex, import the phased genotypes again.
Affected and carrier status on the members that define the disease haplotype.

An inheritance model (if none is set, CoGA assumes recessive when a member is marked as a carrier, otherwise dominant) and a region of interest at the disease locus. Without an ROI there are no embryo calls.
P1 and P2 (blues) are the father's homologs, M1 and M2 (greens) the mother's. Untransmitted (grey) is a relative's homolog that was not passed down, or one CoGA could not place.

The disease haplotype has a line under the band: solid red (Affected) for a dominant or X-linked model, dashed orange (Carrier) for a recessive one. On the genome overview the line appears only on the ROI's chromosome.
The marker dots are the raw phased markers. Use them to check that a colour change is a real recombination and not phasing noise. On a very large region they are hidden: zoom in.

⚠ phasing QC — the embryo's phasing QC at the ROI does not meet its thresholds, counted over the ROI and 1 Mb on each side: at least 50 informative sites, a Mendelian error rate of at most 2%, and at least 6 markers on each flank of the ROI on each parent's side the call reads. The tooltip names each measure, its value and its threshold. The call stands: check it in the ROI markers before you rely on it. These thresholds are provisional, to be confirmed by the laboratory director and QA. At an X-linked locus a man is counted with his one X: a son against his mother alone.

⚠ both homologs — the embryo's markers at the ROI mix both of a parent's homologs, as where it carries both (a trisomy of that chromosome). Its haplotype blocks show only one of them, so the embryo is not called: it reads Uninformative, and its haplotype tracks show no risk state. The tooltip gives the share of markers off one homolog. Read its copy-number and APCAD tracks. The threshold (more than 10%, over at least 20 markers, on a parent's side the call reads) is provisional too.
⚠ QC not counted — no phasing QC was counted at the ROI, so the call was not checked against the thresholds; the tooltip says why.
⚠ recombination — a haplotype change inside the ROI or within 250 kb of it; the call may not hold across the locus.

⚠ phase corrected — CoGA undid a phase switch in a parent's haplotypes inside or close to the ROI. Where the phase switched is known only roughly, so the call across the locus is less certain: review the ROI markers.
⚠ uninformative — no call is made: no disease haplotype could be resolved, or the embryo's haplotype does not cover the ROI.

⚠ sex unknown — an X-linked recessive call depends on the embryo's sex, which is not recorded. The embryo then reads Affected / at risk or Uninformative, and the warning gives the call for a son and for a daughter. Record the sex to resolve it.
