monogenic-nipt.title: Monogenic NIPT
monogenic-nipt.summary: Screen a pregnancy for single-gene disorders from maternal-plasma cfDNA and a paternal sample: set it up, read the page, print the report.
paragraphs: Monogenic NIPT screens a pregnancy for single-gene disorders from cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in maternal plasma, with a sample from the father. The fetus is never sequenced: its genotype is inferred from the cfDNA allele fractions and the fetal fraction (FF), the share of the cfDNA that comes from the fetus.

In Family builder, tick Monogenic NIPT (cfDNA from maternal plasma). Add the father, the cfDNA sample as the mother (mark it cfDNA (maternal plasma)) and the fetus as the proband. A package import does the same when its package says analysis_type: monogenic_nipt. The family page then shows a Monogenic NIPT button.

The data is the NIPT-M pipeline's output: a single-sample VCF of the plasma and one of the father, with a per-target coverage table for each (coverage_<sample>.txt). The package import finds them by the sample names of the PED. One combined VCF with a father column and a cfDNA column works as well. The calls must carry FORMAT/AD.

The built-in presets De novo, Paternal, inherited and Recessive (both parents carrier) set a view with high or moderate impact and a gnomAD frequency of 1% or less (a ClinVar pathogenic record overrides the frequency); De novo also leaves out ClinVar benign and likely benign. The page opens on De novo on the Mendeliome panel, named under the presets as Active filter: De novo, Mendeliome panel (default), as on the small-variant page. Pick a narrower panel if you need one. A link with its own filters, such as Back to NIPT, opens on those.

NIPT report, at the right of the header beside Report, opens a printable summary: the fetal fraction, the quality checks, the coverage of the targets in scope, and the classified variants grouped as De novo in fetus, Dominant, transmitted, Recessive / biallelic risk and Other categories.
Print report prints it.

Sign out NIPT analysis on the NIPT report is the analytical sign-off. It freezes the analysis into the family's signed record, which the EPD report refers to by its report code. It is the family's own sign-out, with the same checks and report code: the family has one signed record whether you sign out here or from the family report. The record holds the NIPT results as CoGA computed them: the fetal fraction and the quality checks, the coverage, and each variant tagged report with its category, reads and probabilities.
blocks: The header shows the fetal fraction, its 95% confidence interval and the number of sites it rests on, a Low-confidence FF chip when the estimate is weak, and the filter funnel (Total, Quality-filtered, Artifact-filtered, Analysed). As on every family page, it warns Import incomplete while a data import has left the family partly loaded or has not finished, and Not validated for clinical use for a family outside the validated scope.

Quality checks come first: the fetal fraction (with the per-site median and the de novo window), the fetal sex from the father's X alleles and from the chrY coverage, paternity, the maternal plasma sample, the coverage of the capture targets and why cfDNA calls failed the quality filter. The section opens folded, with one verdict: Pass when every check passed, Fail as soon as one failed, Warning otherwise (a check that could not run counts as a warning). Click it for the details. A failed paternity check means another father or a sample mix-up: do not read the variants.

The filters are the small-variant page's Pathogenicity, Annotations, In silico, Frequency, Locations and Exclude filters and its review tags (Review and curation: the tags, not the classification or saved notes), plus Maternal/fetal categories (tick any of the eight; each shows its count), a minimum classification confidence, Hide recurrent low-VAF calls (below) and an Inheritance view: De novo in the fetus: calls in the fetal window without a supported call in the father, triaged and ranked by score. List de novo candidates of priority picks high, high and medium, or every candidate. Paternal, inherited by the fetus and Maternal, inherited by the fetus: each parent's alleles with the probability that the fetus inherited them. Also list the alleles the fetus did not inherit adds the rest. Recessive: both parents carriers: the genes where both parents are heterozygous for an allele, in a table with the fetal risk per gene.

De novo in the fetus: calls in the fetal window without a supported call in the father, triaged and ranked by score. List de novo candidates of priority picks high, high and medium, or every candidate.

Paternal, inherited by the fetus and Maternal, inherited by the fetus: each parent's alleles with the probability that the fetus inherited them. Also list the alleles the fetus did not inherit adds the rest.
Recessive: both parents carriers: the genes where both parents are heterozygous for an allele, in a table with the fetal risk per gene.

Each variant carries its category, the plasma reads, the father's genotype, the probabilities that the fetus inherited the paternal or maternal allele or is homozygous, a de novo candidate's priority, any flags and Other cfDNA samples: in how many other cfDNA samples of the assay, in every project, its allele is called, and how (maternal, the father's allele, or an unexplained low-VAF call that no parent explains, the mark of a recurrent artefact). This sits next to the usual annotation, tags and ACMG classification. As on the small-variant page, the diseases its gene is linked to are named under the card's heading.

Hide recurrent low-VAF calls leaves out the variants that are an unexplained low-VAF call in more than the number of other cfDNA samples you give. A variant that ClinVar may call pathogenic, or that is common in the population, stays listed, marked kept by the recurrence filter. The filter narrows the list only; the fetal fraction and the classifications do not change. The count grows with every pregnancy imported, so it is also how you find candidates for the assay's artifact list.

On-target coverage, under the variants, gives the median depth over the capture targets of the panel and genes you selected (every target without a selection) and how many genes have a weak target: a mean below 300× or a base without coverage, where a fetal variant can be missed. Coverage details opens the coverage page: the genes below target and above it, each opening to its targets and their depth. Back to NIPT returns to the NIPT page with your filters.

Read the probabilities, not only the category. A de novo or paternal allele shows clearly at any fetal fraction. Whether the fetus inherited a maternal allele needs depth and a fair fetal fraction: check its probability. The recessive risk assumes both alleles are pathogenic and, at two sites, in trans; an allele without a population frequency (every MNV) is noted.
Its footer names when it was made and the CoGA version that made it.
Its Scope names the panel and genes you selected; your other filters do not apply.
It lists up to 500 variants. When there are more, it says how many it lists of how many and where the list stops, on screen and in print. Narrow the scope with a panel or a gene.
An Import incomplete or Not validated for clinical use warning heads it, on screen and in print, whenever the family page would show one.
The report is live, never the signed record. It says so beside the latest signed version, and every printout starts with Draft or Not the signed report.
Tag the variants you report first. Show reported (N), in the NIPT page's header, lists them before you sign out: the variants tagged report, with every other filter cleared.

A tagged variant the analysis does not classify (not in the family's NIPT data, on the assay's artifact list, or without a call in the plasma) is in no list. The page names it above the list with the reason, as the signed record does.
Besides the Sample QC, a NIPT quality check that failed (no fetal-fraction estimate, fetal-sex signals that disagree, or male DNA as the maternal plasma) stops the sign-out until you record a reason.
Afterwards the signed version opens, with its report code. The NIPT report then shows Amend sign-out and says whether the data still matches the signed version.
Only a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator signs out. For an analyst, a viewer or a reader the button is disabled, here and on the report, and says why.

Screening, not diagnosis. A NIPT call must be confirmed by an invasive diagnostic test. Check the fetal fraction and the quality checks before you read any variant, and a de novo candidate's absence in the father and its reads before you act on it.

explorers.title: Gene, variant and CNV explorers
explorers.summary: Questions beyond one case: a gene profile, a variant across the cohort, and the catalogue of clinical CNVs.
paragraphs: Three explorers answer questions beyond a single case. Open them from the menu under the arrow at the right of the top bar, or from the dashboard.

A profile per gene: the transcripts, badged MANE Select, MANE Plus Clinical, RefSeq Select and Ensembl Canonical; constraint metrics (pLI, LOEUF, missense constraint); disease associations with ClinGen and GenCC evidence and OMIM links; the Monarch gene–disease associations (see Phenotypes, panels and phenotype matching); and links to the main external resources.

Every small variant across the projects you can access, one row per variant: gene, variant, classification, consequence and tags, with the number of carriers (het and hom) and of families. A variant reviewed in more than one family shows the most severe classification of those reviews, and the tags of all of them. Each review counts with the class the family page shows for it, also when it holds only a class tag such as Likely pathogenic - class 4. Of two reviews of the same class, the row shows the one saved last. The classification filter keeps a variant one of whose reviews shows that class, as on the family page, so it also finds a review classified by its class tag alone. The row may show a more severe class, from another family's review.
The catalogue of known clinical CNVs (syndromes and recurrent regions) for an assembly. Search by name, chromosome or type; each row shows the CNV, cytoband, location, size and ClinVar P/LP.
blocks: ACMG secondary finding says whether the gene is on the ACMG secondary-findings list that CoGA ships: On ACMG SF v3.3, with the phenotype, category, inheritance, variants to report and footnotes the list gives for the gene, or Not on ACMG SF v3.3. Not checked means the list could not be read for this gene.

ClinGen dosage curation gives ClinGen's haploinsufficiency and triplosensitivity curations of the gene, the date of the curation and a link to ClinGen's report. The item with an HI score is ClinGen's haploinsufficiency score as dbNSFP carries it.
Filter as on the family page (gene, consequence, ClinVar, frequency, in-silico scores), plus tags and classification — for example every variant tagged Report.

The annotation filters work as on the family page: they must all hold on one transcript of the variant, one of the in-silico predictors you set is enough, and MANE only keeps nothing on GRCh37 or T2T (see Small-variant prioritisation).

Every filter is read for each family as its own family page reads it, so a row counts the carriers and families of the family pages that show the variant. When two families' files were annotated differently (two VEP runs), a filter on the gene, consequence, ClinVar or frequency counts only the family whose own annotation meets it.

A row counts only the samples their family shows. A member taken out of a family keeps its calls in that family's imported data, but is not counted there or listed among its carriers; the genotype filter neither offers nor reads a sample that no family shows.
A location reads the chromosome with or without chr, and the mitochondrion as chrM, M or MT.

Genotype per sample keeps the variants that sample carries as het, hom or either (a haploid call, on chrM or a male's X, counts as hom). The row still counts every carrier in your projects, not only that sample's family.

A gene panel works as on the family page too: it keeps the variants of its genes and the variants in its regions (PanelApp's regions for the assembly, and each gene's position in the gene reference), so a variant whose annotation names its gene differently is kept. This holds for a panel of any size, the Mendeliome included.
Click a het, hom or family count to see the carriers per family, with links to their family pages.
Imputed calls are left out unless you tick Include imputed variants (GLIMPSE2 / SHAPEIT).

Download CSV exports the filtered variants with their annotation, up to 50,000 rows. A file that misses matches has TRUNCATED in its name, and the page says why: more variants matched than the 50,000 rows (narrow the filters), or the tag or classification filter matched more than the 200,000 variants one search takes (filter on fewer tags or classifications).

Cytoband is the band the knowledgebase states. Where it states none, CoGA reads the bands the region spans from the assembly's cytobands, the ones the ideogram draws. An assembly without cytobands, such as T2T, shows none.

ClinVar P/LP, for example 12 loss · 3 gain, counts the pathogenic or likely pathogenic ClinVar copy-number variants that overlap the region by at least 30% both ways, as counted when the knowledgebase was built.
"—" means that the knowledgebase was built without ClinVar: not recorded, not zero.
Click a CNV for its detail page, with its description, the supporting ClinVar records and links to OMIM and DECIPHER. The same page opens when you click a clinical CNV in the viewers.
Counts follow your access. The variant explorer's cohort counts include only the projects you can see: your own, or every project for a superuser or an administrator.

administration.title: Administration
administration.summary: The admin dashboard: reference data, users and access, data management, variant configuration, database operations and audit logs.
paragraphs: Administrator tools sit behind admin access. Admin, in the top-bar menu, or Open admin dashboard on the dashboard opens the admin dashboard, grouped in six areas. A superuser sees five of its pages: Gene panels, Sequencing QC thresholds, Package import, Variant tags and Preset filters. Every other page is an administrator's alone.
blocks: Species & assemblies — the genome builds and their reference data (cytobands, genes, clinical CNVs, segmental duplications, DGV), with each dataset's status. Refresh the human gene information, rebuild the clinical-CNV knowledgebase, load the pinned DGV release, or upload a reference file. Adding GRCh37 or GRCh38 starts the clinical-CNV build and the DGV load for it.

Gene panels — the panel catalogue: create panels, import them from PanelApp, and see their genes. A PanelApp search shows each panel's genes, regions and STRs by confidence level (green, amber, red). A panel can be imported green only, green + amber, or green + amber + red: each is a panel of its own, to filter on apart. Deleting a panel asks first, naming the panel and its version: its genes, its regions and every archived version go with it.

HPO terminology — the HPO release in use and the SHA-256 of the file it came from, and whether HPO has published a newer one; preview and apply a new release, downloaded from HPO or from a file on the server. The release is the one the file states. A file that states no release, or another than the release you asked for, is refused, and Apply imports only the file the preview showed. A new installation starts on HPO's newest release, downloaded at its first start; when HPO cannot be reached it starts on the release shipped with CoGA, which the page names.

Monarch data — load the Monarch release (gene–disease and disease–phenotype links) that powers phenotype matching and the ranking. A new installation loads the newest release at its first start; load a newer one about monthly. Loading it here also rebuilds the Mendeliome panel; after the first start, build that panel on the Gene panels page.

Repeat catalogue — for each repeat locus, QA's record of TRGT's count there, with the reason, who and when, and the history of these records: a count correction, in repeats, added to TRGT's count before every call at the locus is classified (−1 turns TRGT's 18 into 17; from −20 to 20). It applies whether or not the locus is validated, and TRGT's own count stays shown beside the corrected one. Set count correction changes it; on a validated locus a changed correction is recorded as not validated, until QA validates the locus with it. No locus has one until QA enters it. At FMR1 a constant correction is wrong (TRGT is 1 to 3 low, by the number of AGG interruptions), and the page says so next to the field; whether the locus is validated: TRGT's count, with its correction, is the clinical repeat number. Until it is, the repeat page marks its counts near a boundary (Structural variants, repeats, Paraphase and mtDNA). Each change needs a reason and is kept in the clinical audit trail, with the record before and after. The loci the stored calls name are listed first.

Users — accounts, how each signs in (Microsoft or a password), roles and activation, and each user's projects with their level there (analyst or reader). A colleague's first Microsoft sign-in creates their account: a viewer in no project. Set an account's role in its Role list; each role's tooltip says what it may do. CoGA asks you to confirm; you cannot change your own. The roles, lowest first, each with every right of the ones before it: a viewer reads the records of their projects and changes none; an analyst also analyses them (reviews, tags, classifications, HPO terms, the case's workflow, new families); a supervisor also signs an analysis out; a superuser also has every project, member or not, and the gene panels, variant tags, preset filters, sequencing QC thresholds and package import; an admin has the whole administration. Give the supervisor role only to those the laboratory authorises to sign out. Each account shows when it was added and where it stands. A sign-up, or a first sign-in through the organisation, waits for approval: these accounts come first, and every active administrator gets an e-mail about each when a mail server is set (the page says who, and Send a test mail checks it). Activate the account, or Delete it when it is not relevant; only an account that was never active can be deleted. Deactivate an account to revoke access without deleting its history. Archive one that is not coming back: it is deactivated and leaves the list (tick Show archived accounts to see it), every record still names it, and the same person signing in again makes no new request. Restore brings it back, inactive. You cannot deactivate, archive or delete your own: another administrator does that. Edit, under Project access, sets the account's projects and its level in each: the same memberships as a project's members on Projects & access, set from the account's side. Remove takes a project off; Give access to a project lists a few projects without access at a time (type part of a name to find the others), and a project added starts as an analyst. The dialog lists what the save changes; Save project access saves it all at once. An administrator's or a superuser's row says it has every project, member or not. Every change asks you to confirm it first, and is kept in the audit log. Remove takes a project off; Give access to a project lists a few projects without access at a time (type part of a name to find the others), and a project added starts as an analyst. The dialog lists what the save changes; Save project access saves it all at once. An administrator's or a superuser's row says it has every project, member or not.
Every change asks you to confirm it first, and is kept in the audit log.

When you deactivate an account, an import, a gene reference sync or a clinical CNV knowledgebase rebuild it asked for that has not started yet is not run, and a rebuild not yet loaded loads nothing: its job ends failed, saying why. The same holds once the account loses the role the job needs: superuser or administrator for an import (administrator for one that overwrites a family), administrator for the other two.

Projects & access — the projects (each tied to an assembly) and which families, samples and users belong to them. A user sees only the data of their projects; the cohort counts in the explorers follow the same scope. The members are listed with their level; Remove takes one off. Under them, Add a member lists a few users without access at a time: type part of a name or email to find the others, then Add one (or press Enter when the search finds one user). A member added starts as an analyst. One user's projects are also set on the Users page. An analyst reads the project's records and changes them as far as their role allows: a viewer changes nothing, whatever their level. A reader (a student, say) reads, searches, exports and prints them and saves their own filter presets, but changes nothing and does not see the audit trail. Superusers and administrators have every right in every project, member or not. A case can be assigned to, or reviewed by, an analyst of its projects whose role is not viewer, a superuser or an administrator. A case assigned to someone who became a reader or a viewer keeps them, marked (not eligible), until it is changed. A project that families are linked to cannot be deleted: Delete project is off and says how many. A family's small and structural variants are stored per project, and would stay behind under the deleted one. Sequencing QC thresholds — the warning and error cut-offs per assay behind the Seq. QC chip. None ship by default. A metric without a cut-off reads as not assessed, and a sample with no cut-off for any of its metrics shows Not run on the chip.
Package import — import a family package (see Case setup and data import). A superuser imports too; only an administrator overwrites an existing family.

Variant tags — create, rename, recolour or remove custom review tags, for one project or for everyone. A renamed tag stays on every review and saved filter that uses it. A removed tag stays on the reviews that hold it, marked deleted, and can no longer be added. The built-in and ACMG tags are listed for reference.
Preset filters — the catalogue of the small-variant presets the team uses. Presets are saved on the small-variant page.

Audit logs — every request to the server (who, what, when, the outcome) and every button and link a user clicked. glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.summary: Short definitions of the terms used in CoGA.
blocks: ACMG class — the five-tier variant classification: benign, likely benign, VUS, likely pathogenic, pathogenic.
Affected versus carrier — affected status describes the person, carrier status the genotype. They are recorded separately: an unaffected person can be a carrier.

Analyst / reader — a member's level in a project. An analyst reads and changes the project's records, as far as their role allows; a reader only reads them. A superuser or an administrator has every right in every project.

APCAD — What the abbreviation stands for is to be filled in by the laboratory. A sample's track of allele fractions at single-nucleotide sites. For an embryo, read from the PGT pipeline's VCF, each point is the share of the embryo's reads that carry the alternate allele (0 to 1) at a site where only one parent carries that allele, drawn in that parent's colour. Where the run wrote PCF segments, each parent's segments are drawn over the points. From HiFiCNV the track holds the folded minor allele fraction instead (0 to 0.5), with no parent of origin. The analyst judges an embryo's aneuploidy and large structural variants partly on this track; CoGA makes no call from it.
Assembly — the reference genome build (for example GRCh38) a project uses.
cfDNA — cell-free DNA. In NIPT: the DNA in maternal plasma, mostly maternal with a small fetal part.
ClinVar — the public archive of variant–condition interpretations.
CNV / SV — a copy-number variant is a deletion or duplication; a structural variant is any larger rearrangement, including CNVs, insertions, inversions and translocations.
Compound heterozygous — two different variants in one gene, one on each copy (in trans).
De novo — present in a child and absent in both parents. On a son's X or Y outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, only the mother (X) or the father (Y) passes that chromosome on.
Embryo call — CoGA's derived PGT result for an embryo at the ROI: affected / at risk, carrier, unaffected or uninformative.
EPD — the hospital's electronic patient record. The clinical report is drafted and medically signed there, not in CoGA, and refers to one signed version of the analysis.
Fetal fraction (FF) — the share of the cfDNA that comes from the fetus.
Haplotype, homolog — a homolog is one of a person's two copies of a chromosome; a haplotype is the set of alleles on one homolog.
Heteroplasmy — the fraction of mitochondrial genomes that carry a variant.
HPO — the Human Phenotype Ontology: a hierarchy of clinical phenotype terms, from general to specific.
IBD — identity by descent: a stretch of DNA that two relatives inherited from the same ancestor.
IBS0 — the share of sites where two samples have opposite homozygous genotypes; near zero for a parent and child.
In-silico predictors — CADD, REVEL, SpliceAI, SIFT, PolyPhen and AlphaMissense: scores that predict a variant's effect or splice impact.
Kinship (φ) — a measure of relatedness: about 0.25 for parent and child or siblings, 0.125 for second-degree relatives.
LoF — loss of function: a variant predicted to abolish the gene product (stop gained, frameshift, canonical splice site).
MANE Select / MANE Plus Clinical — agreed reference transcripts for clinical reporting; RefSeq Select and Ensembl Canonical are each database's representative transcript.
Mendelian error — a child's genotype that cannot come from its parents' genotypes; many of them point to a sample swap or a wrong pedigree.
Mendeliome — CoGA's built-in panel of every gene that Monarch says causes a disease or is associated with one; the default scope of the variant pages.
MNV — multi-nucleotide variant: neighbouring bases changed together.
Monarch Initiative — a knowledge graph that links genes, diseases and HPO phenotypes.
NeedLR — the structural-variant annotation tool of the long-read pipeline; its annotations fill the Needlr Annotations filters.
P / LP / B / LB — pathogenic, likely pathogenic, benign, likely benign.
Paraphase — a caller for genes in paralogous or duplicated regions.
PGT — preimplantation genetic testing: testing embryos before transfer.
Phenotype similarity — a score for how well two sets of HPO terms match, weighting rare, specific terms more heavily.
pLI / LOEUF — gene constraint: how intolerant a gene is to loss of function (a high pLI or a low LOEUF means constrained).
popmax — the highest allele frequency in any gnomAD sub-population.
Priority score — the Exomiser-style score that ranks candidates within a family; not a probability.
Recombination — a crossover between the two homologs at meiosis; the haplotype an embryo carries changes at that point.
ROI — region of interest: the gene or locus a family is about.

Role — what an account may do, lowest first, each with every right of the ones before it: viewer (reads), analyst (also analyses), supervisor (also signs out), superuser (also every project, the configuration the analyses read and package import) and admin (the whole administration).

Sign-out — the analytical sign-off in CoGA, by a supervisor, a superuser or an administrator: it closes the analysis and freezes it into a signed version that can never change. The medical sign-off is given on the clinical report, in the EPD.
Trans / cis — two variants on opposite homologs (trans) or on the same homolog (cis).
TRGT — tandem-repeat genotyping, used for repeat-expansion calls.
VAF — variant allele fraction: the share of reads that carry the alternate allele.
VUS tier (hot / warm / cold) — a split of the VUS band by ACMG points: hot 4–5, warm 2–3, cold 0–1.
